gallery.description:
A group of people unveil a large sign that reads “Technical College of the Lowcountry, Beaufort Mather Campus.”
Mather School is located in South Carolina and was added to the Network in 2020. The Mather School was established by Rachel Mather in Beaufort, South Carolina in 1868, and provided education to formerly enslaved women during Reconstruction. After a century of operation, the school closed, but the site today is home to the Technical College of the Lowcountry, Mather Campus.

Strieby Congregational Church, School, and Cemetery Cultural Heritage, and Literary Landmark Site is located in North Carolina and was added to the Network in 2022. This is the site of a church and school founded by Rev Islay Walden, “The Blind Poet of North Carolina” in the 1880s, and a community of formerly enslaved people grew up around the church and school.

gallery.title: File:Reconstruction Era National Historical Park (c9674b9f-3ffa-447f-9114-4ca120cb37f2).JPG
gallery.description:
A brick one-story building with large arched windows and trees surrounding the outside.
Reconstruction Era National Historical Park is located in South Carolina and was added to the Network in 2019. This site interprets the Reconstruction era, 1861-1900 the historic period in which the United States grappled with the question of how to integrate millions of newly freed African Americans into social, political, economic, and labor systems, was a time of significant transformation. The people, places, and events in Beaufort County, South Carolina, reflect on the most important issues of this tumultuous time period.

gallery.description:
A historic marker in front of a large three-story white building.
Hamburg-Carrsville African American Historic District is located in South Carolina and was added to the Network in 2022. This site interprets the history and legacy of the Hamburg Community, which was a Freedman community established after the Civil War, and was the site of the “Hamburg Massacre,” an attack by former Confederates and Red Shirts against Black citizens during the 1876 election period.

gallery.description:
A triangular building set in a field of grass at dusk.
Homestead National Monument is located in Nebraska and was added to the Network in 2019. This site interprets the massive rush of emigration and land redistribution that in occurred in response to the passage of federal legislation. During Reconstruction, many people, including African Americans, moved west to take advantage of land opportunities and to escape the tensions of Reconstruction violence and disputes back east.

gallery.title: File:Beginning Work on Darrah Hall (e1273903-f69a-4fc4-bfc0-ee65970fdabd).JPG
gallery.description:
A white single-story building with scaffolding, caution cones, and people working.
Work began on Darrah Hall in July 2022. The Student Conservation Association (SCA), Maintenance Action Team (MAT), and Historic Preservation Training Center (HPTC) worked to preserve the front porch and siding of Darrah Hall. They also replaced the cedar shingles on the east gable end of the building.
